title: Quasi-finite birational algebras agree locally over a normal point
statement: Let $A\subseteq C$ be commutative integral domains with a common field of fractions $K$, with the inclusion inducing the identity on $K$. Assume that $C$ is a finite-type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ be a prime ideal, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$, and assume that $A\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. If $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is integrally closed in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then the induced local homomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p}\to C_{\mathfrak q}$ is an isomorphism. Here localizations are at complements of the indicated prime ideals [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Stacks Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof of (4), local algebra paragraph identifying the normal base local ring with the quasi-finite source local ring.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$. Regard $R$ and $C_{\mathfrak q}$ as subrings of the given common field $K$: fractions map to their quotients in $K$, and equality there is equality after cross-multiplication, since the rings are domains. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $a\notin\mathfrak p$ implies $a\notin\mathfrak q$, so this realizes the induced map $R\to C_{\mathfrak q}$ as an inclusion.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof of (4), local algebra paragraph; fraction details expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-finite-subalgebra-away] to the given finite-type inclusion $A\subseteq C$ and its quasi-finite prime $\mathfrak q$. It supplies an $A$-subalgebra $B\subseteq C$, finite as an $A$-module, and $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, such that the canonical map $B_g\to C_g$ is an isomorphism. No quasi-finiteness at other primes is required.

For each $b\in B$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] gives a monic equation over $A$. The same equation has coefficients in $R$, so $b\in K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is integral over $R$. Here $\operatorname{Frac}(R)=K$ because $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ and every quotient of elements of $A$ is a quotient of elements of $R$. Normality [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] therefore puts every $b$ in $R$, giving $B\subseteq R$.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof of (4), local algebra paragraph; fraction details expanded.

Write $g=a/s$ in $R$, where $a,s\in A$ and $s
otin\mathfrak p$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $sg=a$ in $C$, since it holds in $K$. If $a\in\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$, primeness of $\mathfrak q$ and $s
otin\mathfrak q$ would force $g\in\mathfrak q$, a contradiction. Thus $a
otin\mathfrak p$ and $g^{-1}=s/a\in R$. Consequently $C\subseteq C_g=B_g\subseteq R$ inside $K$, by the canonical isomorphism of Step 2 and the fraction description [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: For $c\in C\setminus\mathfrak q$, the inclusion $C\subseteq R$ writes $c=a/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$. Again $sc=a$ in $C$; if $a\in\mathfrak p$, primeness forces $c\in\mathfrak q$, a contradiction. Thus $c^{-1}=s/a\in R$. Every fraction $d/c$ defining $C_{\mathfrak q}$ therefore lies in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Along with Step 1 this proves equality of the two subrings of $K$. The inverse sends each $d/c$ to the same quotient in $R$, so it is inverse to the induced local homomorphism in the statement.
